source_text: Quod enim unus facit et ad alios dirigit, non vere hoc omnes fecisse dicuntur; aut enim pertransiit ad eos et ipsi non peccaverunt aut ipsi peccaverunt, quo sermone negotium operationis exprimitur, et ad eos non pertransiit nisi imitatione sola.
pass_a_gloss: For what one does and directs toward others, not truly are all said to have done this; for either it passed through to them and they themselves did not sin, or they themselves sinned, by which speech a business of working is expressed, and it did not pass through to them except by imitation alone.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: What one person does and directs toward others cannot truthfully be described as something they all did. Either it passed to them and they themselves did not sin; or they themselves sinned—a phrase expressing the activity of doing something—and it passed to them only through imitation.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
